name: LongBench
intro: LongBench 是 ACL 2024 的原版中英双语、多任务长上下文理解基准（不同于后续 LongBench v2）。标准集含 21 个数据集和 4,750 条测试样本，覆盖单文档问答、多文档问答、摘要、少样本学习、合成任务与代码补全，其中 14 个英文任务、5 个中文任务和 2 个代码任务；论文报告英文平均 6,711 词、中文平均 13,386 字，固定 HF 工件重算值则为 6,666.63 词和 13,338.71 字。LongBench-E 从同一候选池的 13 个英文/代码数据集按 0–4k、4–8k、8k+ 三档均匀采样，共 3,668 条。官方代码使用数据集专用提示、首尾保留式中间截断、贪心解码及 F1、ROUGE-L、分类/数字解析准确率或代码编辑相似度。
org: Tsinghua University, Zhipu.AI, Institute of Automation CAS
build_method: 公开测试集改造, 三名博士生构建 MultiFieldQA, 证据与干扰文档重组, 训练示例抽样, 合成检索计数, 代码补全抽样
metric: 逐数据集：QA F1, ROUGE-L, 论文 CLS/评测器按匹配标签数给 1/n, 论文 EM/评测器按匹配数字占比计分, 代码编辑相似度；六类宏平均
language: 英文, 中文, 代码
task_type: 长文档问答, 摘要, 少样本学习, 合成任务, 代码补全
eval_feature: 六类任务, 数据集专用提示与输出上限, 中间截断保留首尾, 贪心解码, 多参考答案取最大值, LongBench-E 长度分档
variant: Original LongBench and LongBench-E (not LongBench v2)
openness_en: Public (MIT repository; no license metadata on the HF dataset card)
task_type_en: Long-document QA, summarization, few-shot learning, synthetic tasks, code completion
build_method_en: Adapt public test data, author MultiFieldQA with three PhD annotators, compose evidence and distractor documents, sample training demonstrations, synthesize retrieval/counting tasks, and sample code completion
eval_feature_en: Six task families, dataset-specific prompts and output caps, middle truncation preserving both ends, greedy decoding, maximum over references, and LongBench-E length bins
intro_en: LongBench is the original ACL 2024 bilingual, multitask benchmark for long-context understanding, distinct from the later LongBench v2. Its standard release contains 21 datasets and 4,750 test examples across single-document QA, multi-document QA, summarization, few-shot learning, synthetic tasks, and code completion: 14 English tasks, five Chinese tasks, and two code tasks. The paper reports means of 6,711 English words and 13,386 Chinese characters, while recomputation from the pinned HF artifact gives 6,666.63 words and 13,338.71 characters. LongBench-E uniformly samples 13 English/code datasets from the same candidate pool into 0–4k, 4–8k, and 8k+ bins for 3,668 examples. Official evaluation uses dataset-specific prompts, middle truncation that preserves both ends, greedy decoding, and task-specific F1, ROUGE-L, classification/digit-parsing accuracy, or code edit similarity.
metric_en: Per dataset: QA F1, ROUGE-L, paper CLS/evaluator 1 over matched labels, paper EM/evaluator fraction of matching digits, and code edit similarity; macro-average across six categories

drawio_review_note: Paper-alignment review passed against arXiv:2308.14508v2 and ACL 2024 Long Paper 172, especially Sections 3.1–3.2 and 4.1, Tables 1, 3, 7, and 8, and Appendices A–B; official THUDM/LongBench commit 2e00731f8d0bff23dc4325161044d0ed8af94c1e (LongBench/task.md, config/dataset2prompt.json, config/dataset2maxlen.json, pred.py, eval.py, and metrics.py); and public Hugging Face revision 5e628be450b7e67fb7ae6e201bd6d8f7056f7672, whose data.zip LFS object is cb45b11a4133c6bc1d6a44b0f8e701335ff1e543195db1103472e575857f7f64. Table 1 fixes the 21-task composition, sample counts, mean lengths, metrics, and languages: NarrativeQA 200/18,409 English words; Qasper 200/3,619 words; MultiFieldQA-en 150/4,559 words; MultiFieldQA-zh 200/6,701 Chinese characters; HotpotQA 200/9,151 words; 2WikiMultihopQA 200/4,887 words; MuSiQue 200/11,214 words; DuReader 200/15,768 characters; GovReport 200/8,734 words; QMSum 200/10,614 words; MultiNews 200/2,113 words; VCSUM 200/15,380 characters; TREC 200/5,177 words; TriviaQA 200/8,209 words; SAMSum 200/6,258 words; LSHT 200/22,337 characters; PassageCount 200/11,141 words; PassageRetrieval-en 200/9,289 words; PassageRetrieval-zh 200/6,745 characters; LCC 500/1,235 code words; and RepoBench-P 500/4,206 code words. This yields category totals of 750, 800, 800, 800, 600, and 1,000, hence 4,750 examples, 14 English tasks, five Chinese tasks, and two code tasks; the paper-level means are 6,711 English words and 13,386 Chinese characters. Recomputing length from the pinned HF data.zip gives 6,666.63 English/code words and 13,338.71 Chinese characters; notable task drift includes GovReport 8,169.4 vs paper 8,734, MuSiQue 11,017.7 vs 11,214, QMSum 10,545.9 vs 10,614, and VCSUM 15,147.0 vs 15,380. Figure 1 also labels summarization as 600, but Table 1 has four 200-example datasets and the stated 4,750 total requires 800, so the diagram follows Table 1 and records Figure 1 as a paper typo. The paper says public tasks use test sets except VCSUM, whereas the pinned repository note says validation or test splits; no extraction scripts or immutable upstream dataset revisions are released, so this split conflict is preserved rather than resolved by guesswork. NarrativeQA, Qasper, GovReport, QMSum, and MultiNews reuse original data with ZeroSCROLLS-style plain-text conversion; VCSUM uses a dedicated template and selected long segments. MultiFieldQA collects multi-domain documents and has three PhD students author definitive-answer questions with randomized evidence placement; Appendix A reports about five minutes per item and 100% cross-validation accuracy. HotpotQA, 2WikiMultihopQA, and MuSiQue retain 2–4 support passages, expand to full Wikipedia passages, add distractors to a maximum length, and randomize order; DuReader combines related and arbitrary distractor documents to 20 documents per question. Few-shot targets use sampled training examples with ranges TREC 100–600, TriviaQA 2–24, SAMSum 10–100, and LSHT 10–40; TriviaQA demonstration passages are filtered below 1,000 words. PassageRetrieval-en and -zh sample 30 passages and ask for the source of a GPT-3.5-Turbo summary. PassageCount samples M in [17,50], N in [2,M], samples with replacement from N unique English-Wikipedia passages, and shuffles. LCC samples next-line completion; RepoBench-P selects XF-F with the Oracle-Filled setup and shuffles cross-file snippets including the annotated gold snippet. Candidate records contain input, context, answers, length, dataset, language, all_classes, and _id; length counts the first three fields in words for English/code and characters for Chinese. From that common candidate pool, random sampling preserves the natural length distribution and produces the 4,750-example standard LongBench, while uniform sampling forms LongBench-E in parallel. LongBench-E is not a post-hoc subset of those 4,750 rows and is not LongBench v2: it selects Qasper, MultiFieldQA-en, HotpotQA, 2WikiMultihopQA, GovReport, MultiNews, TREC, TriviaQA, SAMSum, PassageCount, PassageRetrieval-en, LCC, and RepoBench-P, then samples by word count into 0–4k, 4–8k, and 8k+ bins up to 100 each. Table 8 gives Qasper 100/100/24, MultiFieldQA-en 67/70/13, MultiNews 100/100/94, and 100/100/100 for the other ten datasets, totaling 3,668. Pinned inference fills dataset-specific prompt templates, applies output caps of 32/64/128/512 tokens, tokenizes before model-specific chat wrapping, and if the prompt exceeds model limit M decodes the first M/2 and last M/2 token halves while dropping the middle. TREC, TriviaQA, SAMSum, LSHT, LCC, and RepoBench-P deliberately bypass chat wrappers; generation is greedy, and SAMSum adds newline as an EOS. Model-level cleanup strips XGen whitespace and its Assistant: marker and truncates InternLM at <eoa>. Evaluation then keeps the first line for the four few-shot tasks and the first non-comment line for code, takes the maximum metric over reference answers, averages per dataset, and multiplies by 100. F1, ROUGE-L, classification-label parsing, numeric retrieval/count parsing, and fuzzy code edit similarity are dispatched per dataset. Although Table 1 calls TREC/LSHT Accuracy (CLS), metrics.py scans all class labels appearing in the prediction and awards 1/n when the ground-truth label is among n matches, so it is not strict single-label exact match. Likewise, although Table 1 calls retrieval/count Accuracy (EM), metrics.py extracts every digit and awards the fraction matching the target, so it is not strict whole-string exact match. The paper averages datasets within each of six categories and defines overall as the mean of the six category means; code tasks enter both English and Chinese views. Current eval.py writes per-dataset results and LongBench-E per-bin results but does not itself compute the paper's category/overall aggregates. Release drift is explicit: the current repository root serves LongBench v2 and moves original files under LongBench/; code still loads THUDM/LongBench while that URL now redirects to zai-org/LongBench; task.md contains a stray NQ description and a PasskeyRetrieval-zh typo absent from the 21-task statistics and executable dataset list. The public repository carries MIT, the HF card exposes no license metadata, and the official README contains a static result leaderboard but no submission or versioned-board interface.
